name: Minnesota
overview: Minnesota has separate refundable renter and homeowner programs; the homeowner program includes a special refund for sharp tax increases.

programs.name: Renter’s Credit
programs.ageRule: All ages, subject to other eligibility rules.
programs.incomeDefinition: Federal AGI with prescribed spouse/nonresident adjustments and subtractions for dependents, age/disability, and eligible stipend payments.
programs.formulaSummary: The annual credit table applies income-dependent thresholds, copayments and caps to 17% of qualifying rent; subsidized-rent adjustments may apply.
programs.application: File M1RENT and M1REF with the Minnesota income-tax return; include Certificates of Rent Paid.
eligibilityNotes: A qualifying Minnesota resident renting tax-paying or qualifying payments-in-lieu property.
Mobile-home lot rent alone goes through M1PR, not M1RENT.
interactions: Income-tax filing replaced the separate renter refund starting with 2024 rent.
The same rent does not qualify under both M1RENT and homeowner lot-rent claims.

programs.name: Homeowner’s Homestead Credit Refund — regular
programs.ageRule: All ages, subject to other eligibility rules.
programs.incomeDefinition: 2025 household income under M1PR, with specified dependent, retirement, senior and disability subtractions.
programs.maximumBenefit: The 2025 M1PR table has a $3,480 base maximum. Revised line 17a adds 14.88% of the line 17 refund under the 2026 law.
programs.formulaSummary: Income-banded thresholds, claimant copayments and maximum refunds apply to qualifying property taxes. Revised 2025 M1PR line 17a adds 14.88% of line 17.
programs.application: File Form M1PR separately from the income-tax return.
eligibilityNotes: Own and occupy the qualifying homestead on January 2, 2026.
Homestead classification and no delinquent property taxes (or qualifying arrangement) required.
interactions: May qualify for both regular and special refunds.
programs.programYear: 2025 household income with property taxes payable in 2026; claim generally filed in 2026.

sources.title: 2025 M1PR instructions, revised June 2026: additional refund on line 17a

programs.name: Homestead Credit Refund — special
programs.ageRule: All ages, subject to other eligibility rules.
programs.maximumBenefit: $1,000 under the 2025 M1PR instructions revised in June 2026.
programs.formulaSummary: A refund of qualifying increases above the statutory percentage threshold; 2025-to-2026 net tax must rise more than 12% and at least $100, excluding improvements.
eligibilityNotes: Must own and occupy the same home January 2, 2025 and January 2, 2026.
interactions: Can accompany a regular refund, subject to M1PR coordination.
programs.programYear: 2025 M1PR compares taxes payable in 2025 and 2026.

laterChanges: A law enacted in May 2026 retroactively increased regular 2025 homeowner refunds. Revised M1PR line 17a adds 14.88% of the refund from the existing table.
researchNotes: The regular homeowner and renter programs use different income concepts and housing-tax years.
The $3,480 homeowner table maximum precedes the additional line 17a refund in the revised 2025 return.
